missions.title: On Your Bike
missions.where: Your Flat → The Arches (Hackney Central)
missions.hook: Mo bangs on the door: rent is due Friday, and Pat "wants a word". Pat wants two bikes by tonight. Nothing fancy. Kez will show you where.

objectives.text: Get round to The Arches on Morning Lane
Nick two bikes (Graft against the lock)
Sell two bikes to Auntie Pat

missions.next: Pat has a buyer for something better: Mission 2.
missions.decision: Complete the theft, buy a substitute, return a recognised bicycle or give Pat an honest partial delivery. Whoever loses an object becomes a recurring person.
missions.consequences: A completed order opens CH2 and repeat working access to HC7. A disputed bike becomes a recovery obligation; the new workshop remains available through Spanner even if payment is reduced.
missions.campaign:
The job. Mo wants the rent and Pat wants two saleable bicycles. Preserve the existing opening, fencing proceeds and GBP 40 order bonus; the new storehouse becomes the first expansion of the crew's working world.

Scenes. FL4 and AR4 establish the debt and order. At LF1.1, a fictional cycling event leaves valuable bicycles beside the entrance; taking one leads to a recognition scene in LF1.2. In HC7.2, Spanner inspects the haul while a claimant arrives at the roller door.

Route and checks. HC / DA / LF / DA / HC. Graft for acquisition; Front for the claimant; Moves for a chase.

Use existing fencing proceeds and GBP 40 order bonus in place of the flat fee.
missions.campaignTwist: Daz follows the second bicycle into the storehouse yard. Pat wants the order settled before the buyer's collection, with the true ownership still in dispute.
missions.gm:
Start everyone in Your Flat. Walk out through Chicken Palace onto Mare Street; The Arches are round the corner on Morning Lane (the door on the Hackney map, or ride straight up to the yard).

Pat gives the order on the phone (Ask Pat for an order) or in person. Street Life puts chained bikes on every map; Kez's tip-offs are a map or two away. This is the mission to teach the lock roll, Heat (the first time someone watches), and selling at The Arches — Pat whispers an offer with a Sell button when they pull up.

GM Screen: Street → Kez's tip-off bike spawns a target near them; Checks → Spot the Old Bill before they cut the lock.
missions.twist: One of the bikes belongs to a Lea Boy. He saw. Next session he wants it back — or Stretch does.

missions.title: The Whippet
missions.where: Broadway Market (Haggerston & London Fields)
missions.hook: Pat has a buyer for a Carbon Whippet road bike — £1,800 new. The Lycra lot chain them up outside the coffee places on Broadway Market and along the canal.

objectives.text: Get to Broadway Market
Check the rack for a bait bike (Savvy, Hard)
Bring Pat a Carbon Whippet

missions.next: The Lea Boys hear Pat is paying well. Mission 3.
missions.decision: Steal or purchase the correct bike, negotiate a different sale, switch buyers or deliver an agreed substitute. A secret substitution can earn cash and create a later dispute.
missions.consequences: Pat recognises the accepted delivery once. LF4 and HB4 become recurring buyer contacts, while a witnessed theft gives Vale an ordinary lead into LD1.
missions.campaign:
The job. Pat has a buyer for the Carbon Whippet. The recovery begins at the established Broadway Market coffee rack, then expands into a private inspection and competing offers.

Scenes. At EX-BROADWAY, identify the promised bicycle among a bait bike and a disputed sale. LF4.2 hosts the fictional buyer's inspection. AR3 provides the workshop test; at HB4.2, a collector makes a competing cash offer before the original buyer returns.

Route and checks. BG / HR / LF / DA / HC / CL / SN / HB. Savvy for identification; Graft for the score; Front for the sale.
missions.campaignTwist: Evie Slate has already promised the bicycle to another client. After the inspection, one buyer changes the meeting and the other offers immediate money.
missions.gm:
The lock is Hard. Bolt cutters make it Medium; the angle grinder makes it Easy — but it shrieks, and Broadway Market on a Saturday is full of phones (witnessed: +1 Heat).

If the owner comes back mid-job: Blag Your Way In ("I'm with the council, mate") or Leg It down the towpath. The Regent's Canal towpath runs west to Haggerston: bikes only, no police cars.
missions.twist: DS Vale has put a tracker in a bait bike on the same rack. Spot it (Savvy, Hard) or nick the bait — and a unit turns up at The Arches next session.

missions.title: Lights and Sirens
missions.where: Morning Lane → Wick Road → Hackney Wick
missions.hook: The Lea Boys have driven off with Pat's van of stripped frames from outside The Arches. Pat wants it back before it crosses the Lea.

objectives.text: Get some wheels — fast
Catch the van before Hackney Wick
Get the van back to The Arches
Deal with Stretch: pay him off, fight him, or grass him to DS Vale

missions.next: The Lea Boys come back mob-handed: Mission 4.
missions.decision: Recover the van by pursuit, steal it back during the fictional exchange, buy its release or settle the claim with Stretch. Decide whether Pat receives every frame.
missions.consequences: An accepted recovery earns Pat's award and opens HM7's receiving hall. The crate's clearance papers point to HB8; supporting Stretch changes who will negotiate in LB2.
missions.campaign:
The job. The Lea Boys have taken Pat's van of stripped frames. Keep the established Morning Lane to Waterden to Bow Breakers recovery, then open the wider depot network.

Scenes. AR5 supplies the last inventory. A driver in WW3.2 identifies the departure. EX-MORNING and EX-WATERDEN carry the handover or vehicle chase; EX-BREAKERS is the original recovery destination. A missing crate has already been booked onward to HM7.2.

Route and checks. HC / WW / HC / WS / VW / OF / VW / WW / HM. Wheels for pursuit; Graft for recovery; Front for a settlement.
missions.campaignTwist: Daz moves the van as a second buyer arrives at Waterden. If it escapes, its new holder offers a paid rendezvous at the night shed.
missions.gm:
Steal something fast, or "borrow" the police area car parked on Mare Street (+3 Heat if a copper sees). Chase the van east along Morning Lane → Wick Road: each round the driver rolls Wheels against the van's driver (Opposed on the GM Screen). Track a gap from 2: a win closes it, a loss opens it; 0 = boxed in, 5 = gone.

The clever route: from the stolen area car, run ANPR on every van you pass. GM: put a marker on the van's token and the scanner flags it.

Ending on the Hertford Union bridge: Stretch and two Lea Boys. Use the Combat Console if it kicks off; the GM Screen's NPC tab can place more lads.
missions.twist: Grass Stretch to DS Vale and Pat will hear about it. She does not like grasses, even useful ones.

missions.title: Lea Boys
missions.where: The Arches, Morning Lane
missions.hook: Three in the morning. Mopeds outside The Arches, a brick through Pat's window, and somebody pouring petrol under the shutter.

objectives.text: Hold The Arches
Find out who sent them (Get Someone Talking)
Send the Lea Boys a message back

missions.next: Pat wants to move up to cars: Mission 5. And someone has been talking to the police: Mission 8.
missions.gm:
A fight in the yard. Place four Lea Boys (GM Screen → NPCs → Spawn, twice) and start a fight in the Combat Console. One has a Petrol Bomb: throw the hazard at whoever is nearest the shutter. Police turn up after three rounds if anyone fires a gun.

The one left standing talks: it was Stretch, but someone told Stretch where Pat keeps the ledger. Somebody close to Pat is talking.
missions.twist: The petrol under the shutter was not the Lea Boys' idea. Somebody paid for it.

missions.title: Chop Chop
missions.where: Bow Breakers Yard, Roman Road (Old Ford & Bow)
missions.hook: Pat introduces you to Big Den at Bow Breakers Yard. He wants a hot hatch, an estate or a hybrid — anything that sells for parts. Today.

objectives.text: Nick a car worth having (Fiester ST, Volvagen, Pious, Brixton Bruiser…)
Lose any Heat on the way
Deliver it to Bow Breakers Yard

missions.next: Hot Wheels (Mission 7) when the car jobs get serious.
missions.gm:
Cars are a step up: locks are Medium to Hard, and a relay box or key programmer (Uncle sells them from Rep 2) makes them two bands easier. A car on the street has a plate: drive past a patrol and the ANPR pings it (Clocked).

Bow Breakers is on the Old Ford & Bow map: pull up in the yard and Big Den makes an offer with a Sell button.
missions.twist: The car belongs to one of Uncle's regulars. Uncle will want to talk about it (Mission 6).

missions.title: Uncle's Errand
missions.where: Uncle's Cafe (Bethnal Green) → Roman Road Market
missions.hook: Uncle runs a café in Bethnal Green with two menus. A stallholder on Roman Road owes him £500. Uncle would like it collected, politely if possible.

objectives.text: Get to Uncle's Cafe
Collect the £500 at Roman Road Market
Get back without being dipped or nicked
Hand Uncle his money

missions.next: Uncle's big idea: Mission 9, Westfield.
missions.gm:
The stallholder (GM Screen → NPCs → Shopkeeper) has a story: his daughter is sick, the stall was robbed, the money is "next week". Get Someone Talking, Scare Them Off or Haggle — or pay it yourself and keep the favour.

On the way back: GM Screen → Street → Pickpocket. Losing Uncle's money is a bad start with Uncle.
missions.twist: Uncle's "other menu" opens to you after this — and from Rep 2, the room out the back.

missions.title: Hot Wheels
missions.where: Haggerston → Kwik Spray → Bow Breakers
missions.hook: A Range Ruler SUV is waiting in a car park off Kingsland Road. It has a tracker, the owner has friends in the police, and Kwik Spray closes in an hour.

objectives.text: Pick up the Range Ruler
Lose the unmarked car on your tail
Respray it at Kwik Spray Bodyshop
Deliver it to Bow Breakers Yard

missions.next: Vale makes her move: Mission 8.
missions.gm:
The moment they drive off, set Heat to 2 (GM Screen → Police & Heat). An unmarked car follows (place a Patrol car). Lose the Police or Lose a Tail; the respray clears Heat if no unit sees them go in.

Kwik Spray is on the Haggerston & London Fields map. The respray costs £400 for a car: Pat will pay it back, eventually.
missions.twist: The tracker is not the owner's. It is DS Vale's.

missions.title: Vale
missions.where: Stoke Newington custody suite
missions.hook: DS Vale picks one of you up on a "routine matter" and buys you a coffee in an interview room. She knows about The Arches. She wants the Lea Boys — or Pat.

objectives.text: Get through the interview (Don't Grass)
Decide: give her the Lea Boys, give her nothing, or play her
Cover your tracks before Pat hears

missions.next: The raid: Mission 11.
missions.gm:
Run the interview with the GM Screen: Police → DS Vale Drops By, then Checks → Don't Grass (Hard). Each failure lets something slip; two failures and Vale has enough to raid The Arches (Mission 11 happens sooner and harder).

Giving her the Lea Boys: Mission 12 gets easier (half of Stretch's crew is arrested) but if Pat finds out (Savvy against the player's Front), the crew turns cold.
missions.twist: Vale has a grass inside The Chainring already. She lets the name slip on purpose.

missions.title: Westfield
missions.where: Westfield Stratford
missions.hook: A sports shop in Westfield takes delivery of a limited trainer drop on Thursday. Uncle has buyers for every pair. Smash, grab, mopeds, gone.

objectives.text: Case the shop (Case the Joint)
Get to Westfield Stratford
Grab and go (teamwork: Search the Place)
Get out of Stratford with three stars or less
Stash the gear at the flat

missions.next: The Lea Boys want a reckoning on the Marshes: Mission 10.
missions.gm:
Casing it first earns one fact per success: the security guard's break, the shutter speed, the camera that doesn't work. Each fact makes the grab one band easier.

The grab is a teamwork check; the moment the glass goes, Heat 2 (3 if a guard is hurt). Westfield is next to the Olympic Park: wide roads, few hiding places, and the helicopter comes at three stars.
missions.twist: Stretch's lads are doing the same shop the same night.

missions.title: The Marshes
missions.where: Hackney Marshes
missions.hook: Stretch sends a text: a race across Hackney Marshes at dusk. Winner takes the patch west of the Lea. Loser gives up their bike.

objectives.text: Get to Hackney Marshes
Win the race (three Wheels rolls against Stretch)
Keep your bike

missions.next: Win and Stretch loses face; lose and Pat loses a patch. Either way: Mission 12.
missions.gm:
Three legs: the football pitches, the canal bridge, the Lea towpath. Each is an Opposed Wheels roll against Stretch (GM Screen → Checks → Opposed). Off-road bikes (Trailblazer, Dirt Devil) get +1 on the pitches.

A Proper Mess on the towpath: Come Off the Bike hazard — and the canal is right there (In the Canal).
missions.twist: Stretch cheats: a Lea Boy with a bike chain waits at the bridge.

missions.title: Raid
missions.where: The Arches, Morning Lane
missions.hook: Five in the morning. Kez rings, breathless: three vans on Morning Lane, a dog unit, and DS Vale with a warrant. Pat is still inside with the ledger.

objectives.text: Get to The Arches
Get Pat out the back
Save the ledger (teamwork: Search the Place)
Lose all the Heat

missions.next: Pat wants it finished: Mission 12.
missions.gm:
Set Heat 3 for anyone seen near the yard. Police → Police Dog and Hazards → CS Spray for the officers on the shutter. Officers get out of the vans and take their own turns in the Combat Console (Police AI). Surrendering is an option: Busted, but the ledger might be safe if someone else has it.

If Mission 8 went badly, Vale knows about the back door.
missions.twist: The ledger names the grass. It is someone the players like.

missions.title: Big Night
missions.where: The Lea Boys' lock-up, Leyton
missions.hook: Pat has found where Stretch keeps his stock: a lock-up behind the Leyton Orient ground. Two hundred bikes, a van of parts, and Stretch's cash box. Tonight it ends.

objectives.text: Get to Leyton
Get into the lock-up
Take Stretch's stock — or Stretch
Get everyone home
Face Pat's reckoning with the grass

missions.next: Rep 3 and up: Pat's car jobs, Uncle's back room, and London beyond Hackney.
missions.gm:
The finale. Getting in: Pick a Lock, Break Down a Door, or a ram through the shutter. Inside: Stretch, four Lea Boys and a guard dog. Use the Combat Console; police arrive at Heat 3 after three rounds of gunfire, Trojans at four.

Getting the stock home is a convoy: the Tranzit van (6 seats), bikes on the back. Bow Breakers will take the van; Pat takes the bikes.

Then Pat, the ledger and the grass. Let the players decide. This is the end of "On Your Bike" — and the start of whatever they want The Smoke to be.
missions.twist: DS Vale has been watching the lock-up too. She lets them go — this time.

missions.title: The Frame Room
missions.where: Oddments Lockup · Hackney Marshes Centre · Clifden Crew Garage
missions.hook: Pat bought a Highbury lock-up's worth of frames for buttons: forty bikes, no questions. Then Kez spotted club stickers on half of them and a courier's family papers in a saddlebag. A collector's lorry comes for the lot tomorrow.

objectives.text: Search the Oddments Lockup before the lorry comes
Check the donation story with the organiser at Hackney Marshes Centre
Get the disputed bikes into the Clifden Crew Garage and identify them (Savvy)
Decide: fence the lot, separate the donated bikes, keep the papers or trade profit for a repair contract

missions.gm:
The job. A profitable frame collection includes donated club bikes and a courier's family papers. Pat wants the mixed load sorted before a collector takes the lot.

Scenes. Search HB7.2, compare the donation account with a visiting organiser in WW1.4, then move the disputed bicycles into HC8.2 for identification. HC8.4 also contains a vehicle title that could make the garage a future crew base.

Route and checks. HB / CG / DA / HC / WW / HC. Savvy for inventories; Graft for repairs; Front for competing owners.
missions.decision: Finish a lucrative fence, separate the donation bikes, keep the papers as leverage or trade a smaller profit for a repair contract.
missions.consequences: HB7 becomes a storage contact. Helping the club opens HC8's repair bay and a possible tenancy; keeping the valuable component creates a claimant who can hire a rival.
missions.next: CH5 The Borrowed Winner · NM3 Everything Must Go · RT2 The Watch After Midnight
missions.twist: A removal lorry reaches HB7 after the second enquiry. The collector takes the unclaimed load unless someone pays, delays the handover or contests it.

missions.title: The Borrowed Winner
missions.where: Leyton Orient stadium · Lee Valley VeloPark · Kingsland Courier Arch · The Kenton · Goldsmiths Riding Workshop
missions.hook: A bike nicked off Pat's patch has turned up on a showcase poster at the VeloPark: resprayed, polished and entered to win. Pat could sell it, sell it back, or use it to get Kez's riding workshop a proper contract.

objectives.text: Get an invitation at the Leyton Orient stadium
Find the bike at the Lee Valley VeloPark meet
Trace its courier and the next handover (Kingsland Courier Arch, The Kenton)
Stop the rival rider before the prize-giving (Wheels or Moves)
Decide: deliver the score, return it for a fee, expose the sponsor or buy into the riding workshop

missions.gm:
The job. A stolen high-end bicycle has been entered in a fictional sporting showcase. Pat can sell it, recover it for a fee or use it to secure a legitimate workshop contract.

Scenes. LY1.3 gives the crew an event invitation. ON1.4 holds the bicycle during an invented cycling meet. LF7.3 identifies its courier; WW5.3 reveals the next handover. HR8.2 offers an alternative future for the recovered frame.

Route and checks. LY / ON / ST / VW / WS / LF / DA / HC / WW / HC / DA / LF / HR. Moves for the sporting set piece; Graft for recovery; Front for sponsorship.
missions.decision: Deliver the score, return it for negotiated payment, expose the sponsor's claim or buy into Kez's riding workshop.
missions.consequences: ON1 and LY1 open event work; LF7 supplies dispatch introductions. Funding HR8 creates an asset with running costs, while a private sale leaves the original owner active.
missions.next: CH6 The Shop That Was Already Sold · GE1 The Wrong Provenance · BB2 The Wrong Winner
missions.twist: A rival rider takes the bicycle toward the prize-giving. Run a sporting pursuit, a backstage recovery or a direct bargain before the sponsor presents it.

missions.title: The Shop That Was Already Sold
missions.where: Orchard Lease Office · Essex Dry Goods · Clapton Union Rooms · Stoke Newington Town Hall
missions.hook: A man called Lark has offered Pat a tidy sum to walk away from the Arches, and he talks about the street as if half of it is already empty. It isn't. Pat wants to know who Lark works for before she signs anything.

objectives.text: Find the acquisition schedule at the Orchard Lease Office
Compare offers with the workers at Essex Dry Goods and the Clapton Union Rooms
Confront or bargain with Lark at the property meeting in Stoke Newington Town Hall
Decide: protect Pat alone, build a collective bid, sell the timing evidence or take Meridian's role

missions.gm:
The job. Pat has been offered a private exit while other occupied premises are described as vacant. She wants the intermediary identified and her future settled.

Scenes. HB8.4 contains an earlier acquisition schedule. Workers in DB8.4 describe their offer; CL8.3 holds the matching repair account. At HB5.3, an invented property meeting gives the crew a chance to confront Lark or bargain privately.

Route and checks. HB / CG / DB / CG / DA / HC / CL / SN / HB. Savvy for the date pattern; Front for terms; Bottle under financial pressure.
missions.decision: Protect Pat alone, build a collective bid, sell the timing evidence or support Meridian for a defined role.
missions.consequences: The agreed outcome sets Pat's award. The six-property scheme becomes a supported lead; a private bargain can preserve the shop while creating opposition when neighbours learn its terms.
missions.next: CH7 Who Runs the Arches · BM6 Who Can Promise a Home · MR5 Vacant on Paper
missions.page: CH6 · The Shop That Was Already Sold
missions.twist: Lark offers Pat money before the tenants compare their copies. The meeting closes one offer, but surviving owners and records remain available afterward.

missions.title: Who Runs the Arches
missions.where: Pat's Cycle Repairs · Lea Bridge Social Rooms · Roman Exchange · Tern Wharf Dispatch · MOTH Club
missions.hook: Stretch wants a settlement: who nicks what, where, and who fences it. Pat would rather the crew wrote the terms than had them written for them. Everyone who matters will be in the back room of the MOTH Club on Thursday.

objectives.text: Take Pat's terms in the shop
Find out who backs whom: the Lea Boys' split, the fences at Roman Exchange, the drivers at Tern Wharf
Deal with Daz and the disputed tool chest
Settle the compact at the MOTH Club meeting
Name who pays each genuine debt

missions.gm:
The job. Pat asks the crew to negotiate theft, fencing and recovery territory before Stretch imposes his own settlement.

Scenes. AR1 collects Pat's terms. CL7.2 shows the Lea Boys' split; OF7.3 and HX7.2 establish what fences and drivers support. An invented private meeting in HC5.4 becomes the vote or confrontation settling the compact.

Route and checks. HC / CL / HC / WS / BG / OF / BG / HR / HX / DB / CG / DA / HC. Front for the compact; Muscle and Bottle if violence starts; Savvy for liabilities.
missions.decision: Guarantee a limited compact, back Moth, side with Stretch, take a private monopoly or let the factions split. Name who pays each genuine debt.
missions.consequences: The settlement opens formal negotiation rooms at CL7, OF7 and HX7. Threats, broken promises and public victories create specific future supporters and enemies.
missions.next: CH8 Keys to the Arches · LB7 Who Speaks for the Lea Boys · TU8 The City Still Has to Move
missions.twist: Daz arrives with a disputed tool chest and a younger crew ready to take it back. Resolve the cargo while the meeting's supporters decide whether to stay.

missions.title: Keys to the Arches
missions.where: Chainring Storehouse · Clifden Crew Garage · Glasshouse Saleroom · Meridian Sales Pavilion
missions.hook: Pat is offering you keys. Not to the shutter: to the business. Meridian's last move lands on Morning Lane the same week, and what the Chainring becomes now depends on what you sign, and for whom.

objectives.text: Choose the base and its obligations: the Storehouse or the Clifden garage
Find a buyer or a backer at the Glasshouse Saleroom
Be at the Meridian Sales Pavilion when the papers are signed
Recover the pledged asset before another crew collects it
Decide what the business becomes, and where Pat stands in it

missions.gm:
The job. Pat offers the crew a permanent stake while Meridian's final operation reaches the district. This decides what the business becomes.

Scenes. Choose the base and its obligations at HC7.5 and HC8.4. A fictional sale at CG7.2 supplies a buyer or alternative financier. ST7.4 is the signing opportunity; another crew is collecting one pledged asset.

Route and checks. HC / DA / CG / DA / HC / WS / VW / ST. Front for ownership; Graft for the last practical job; Wheels for the competing collection.
missions.decision: Keep a fencing business, fund a repair cooperative, consolidate territory, accept a buyout or move the operation. Pat negotiates her place in that future.
missions.consequences: Record the crew's actual share, keys, equipment and debt. HC7 or HC8 can become a permanent headquarters; the other remains separately owned unless agreed otherwise.
missions.next: BM8 The Neighbourhood Gets a Vote · MR8 The City on the Brochure · AD8 The Whole City Listening
missions.twist: Rusk's collector and a tenant delegation expect incompatible promises. Resolve one immediate recovery or negotiation during each final-night turn.

missions.title: Borrowed Speakers
missions.where: Queensbridge Sound Store · Cafe OTO · Backspin Studio · Round Chapel
missions.hook: Patch has a listening night booked at the Round Chapel and no speakers. Somebody changed the hire account, and another promoter is already loading the cases into a van.

objectives.text: Find the rig at the Queensbridge Sound Store
Find out who made the replacement booking (the performer at Cafe OTO)
Get into Dead Air's live room at Backspin Studio
Get the night on at the Round Chapel, full rig or not

missions.gm:
The job. Patch needs a sound system for a fictional listening night. Its hire account has been changed and another promoter already has the cases.

Scenes. HR7.2 identifies the speakers. A visiting performer at DA2.3 identifies the replacement booking. DA7.3 opens the fictional station's live room, then HC2.2 hosts the event or showdown with the rival organiser.

Route and checks. HR / LF / DA / HC. Graft for the equipment; Front for the hire dispute; Wheels if the van leaves.
missions.decision: Steal the equipment back, buy replacement hire, move the event or back the rival for a larger fee.
missions.consequences: Honouring the chosen brief opens DA7's working studio and the next station commission. HR7 becomes a hire contact; an unpaid supplier remains a creditor.
missions.next: AD2 The Missing Hour · VC1 The Sound Went Missing · NM2 One Box Two Buyers
missions.twist: A van loads the speakers after the second enquiry. The doors at HC2 open whether the crew has the full rig or agreed a smaller show.

missions.title: The Missing Hour
missions.where: Signature Brew Haggerston · Abney Books · Rio Cinema · Englefield Listening Flat
missions.hook: Nia "Switch" Bell hasn't done her show in three weeks. Now a seller says he has a new message from her on reel — but the station ident on it was retired years ago.

objectives.text: Meet the seller at the station gathering, Signature Brew Haggerston
Find the old sleeve at Abney Books
Hear the reel at the Rio Cinema preview
Have Leon compare it at the Englefield Listening Flat
Decide: broadcast an appeal, buy the reel, trade an exclusive or go public

missions.gm:
The job. Nia Switch Bell has missed several programmes. A seller offers a new message from her containing an ident from an older recording.

Scenes. At HR3.1, a fictional station gathering introduces the seller. SN2.3 finds the old sleeve; DA1.3 hosts an invented preview of the offered reel. In LF8.2, Leon compares what the crew obtained.

Route and checks. HR / LF / DA / SN / DA / LF. Savvy for recordings; Front for sources; Bottle for a public decision.
missions.decision: Broadcast an appeal, buy the reel privately, trade an exclusive or publish an accusation the evidence may not support.
missions.consequences: The old ident opens three recording leads and LF8's listening room. A false public account creates a correction or enemy; losing the reel leaves the sleeve and seller available.
missions.next: AD3 Two Stages One Van · RT1 The Empty Slot · RT4 The Night That Repeated
missions.twist: A rival will buy the reel before the next programme slot. The seller also promises a sighting but cannot explain its date.

missions.title: Two Stages One Van
missions.where: Union Chapel · Hoxton Hall · The Lauriston · North Echo Rehearsal Rooms
missions.hook: Two benefit nights, Union Chapel and Hoxton Hall, have both been promised the same acts and the same rig. A sponsor is offering cash to make it one night. It's raining, and the van leaves at six.

objectives.text: See both programmes: Union Chapel and Hoxton Hall
Recover the disputed fee at the promoters' meeting in The Lauriston
Line up a rehearsal, a replacement act or a recording at North Echo
Decide: combine the nights, honour one promise, sell exclusivity or run your own

missions.gm:
The job. Two fictional benefits have been promised the same performers and sound system. A sponsor offers to pay for exclusivity.

Scenes. CG4.3 and HR2.2 establish the rival programmes. WS4.3 hosts the promoter's meeting, where the disputed fee can be recovered or stolen. ON7.2 supplies a rehearsal, replacement act or surviving recording.

Route and checks. CG / DA / LF / HR / BG / WS / HC / WW / ON. Front for programme deals; Graft for the rig; Wheels for moving the act.
missions.decision: Combine the events, honour one promise, sell exclusivity, take the sponsor's money or run a smaller independent programme.
missions.consequences: The agreed shows open backstage and rehearsal contacts across four interiors. A cancelled act offers later work on different terms; the independence front changes visibly.
missions.next: AD4 Pay to Play · VC3 Cash Before Curtain · BM2 Benefit Night Rain Check
missions.twist: Rain changes both events' capacity and the equipment van is leaving. Each scene commits another resource to one of the bills.

missions.title: Pay to Play
missions.where: Backspin Studio · The Eagle · Lea Bridge Social Rooms · The Shacklewell Arms
missions.hook: Someone rings Dead Air every Friday asking for "Stretch's money". Dee doesn't think Stretch knows. She thinks the caller is wearing a real volunteer's name.

objectives.text: Hear Dee's account at Backspin Studio
Follow the organiser at The Eagle
Get Moth to name the racket at the Lea Bridge Social Rooms
Be there when the collector comes back to the Shacklewell Arms
Decide: pay for peace, expose the impersonator, take the collection back or cut a deal

missions.gm:
The job. A collector demands money for the station's broadcasts using Stretch's name. Dee suspects the caller borrowed a genuine volunteer's identity.

Scenes. DA7.4 establishes Dee's account. A fictional organiser at HX2.2 leads to CL7.3, where Moth can identify the racket. SN5.2 hosts the next listening night and the collector's return.

Route and checks. DA / CG / DB / HX / DB / CG / DA / HC / CL / SN. Front for the protection claim; Savvy for identities; Bottle when the collector returns.
missions.decision: Pay for peace, expose the impersonator, steal back the collection, negotiate a partnership or gain control of a station slot.
missions.consequences: The accepted settlement earns station trust. CL7 and SN5 open further meetings; rivals react through actual witnesses and the false caller still has a sponsor to find.
missions.next: AD5 Somebody Else's Voice · LB3 The Larch Job · BB3 Cash on the Guest List
missions.twist: The real collector arrives and denies the caller's authority. Daz offers another protection deal while the audience gathers.

missions.title: Somebody Else's Voice
missions.where: Grow Hackney · Wallis Tape Rooms · Silt Listening Bunker
missions.hook: A programme went out last night threatening anyone selling Halo, in a voice that sounds exactly like Nia. A visiting artist recognised the hum behind it. Seth the engineer has the rough mix — and a buyer for it.

objectives.text: Match the background sound at the Grow Hackney installation
Get the session history and the original at the Wallis Tape Rooms
Authenticate the sequence at the Silt Listening Bunker
Decide: steal or buy the master, broker it, publish the edit history or bury it

missions.gm:
The job. A threatening programme appears to implicate Nia in the Halo panic. A visiting artist recognises its background sound and Seth has the rough mix.

Scenes. An invented installation at VW4.2 supplies the location sound. VW7.3 and VW7.5 contain the session history and original. HM8.2 provides an independent rehearsal that can authenticate the sequence.

Route and checks. VW / WW / HM. Savvy for corroboration; Graft for recovery; Moves for the departing witness.
missions.decision: Steal or buy the master, broker its release, publish the edit history or conceal it for a faction's money.
missions.consequences: An authenticated comparison supports E3. VW7 and HM8 open deeper archive play; losing the master leaves the artist, cleaner and rehearsal as independent routes.
missions.next: AD6 Open Channel Loud Mouths · RT4 The Night That Repeated · VC5 A Set for Nobody
missions.twist: A buyer has paid Seth for the master and another crew collects it after the second scene. A cleaner with another version leaves tonight.

missions.title: Open Channel Loud Mouths
missions.where: Newington Green Meeting House · The Old Church · Sadler's Wells East
missions.hook: Patch is giving the crew a live programme: two hours, open mic, the whole manor listening. Tenants, dealers, promoters and a sponsor all want to be first on — and one of them has papers that could finish somebody.

objectives.text: Run the planning assembly at Newington Green Meeting House
Fill the first slot at The Old Church
Check the accusation and the papers before they go out (Savvy)
Get the programme out, at The Old Church or Sadler's Wells East
Decide what goes out: the supported case, a partisan night, an exclusive or local work

missions.gm:
The job. Patch gives the crew a live programme. Tenants, dealers, promoters and a sponsor all want the first public account.

Scenes. CG1.2 is the planning assembly. HB2.3 supplies the first performance or listening slot. ST5.4 offers another stage if the sponsor buys the original programme or the crew changes venue.

Route and checks. CG / HB / CG / DA / HC / WS / VW / ST. Front for a live room; Savvy for claims; Bottle for a costly editorial choice.
missions.decision: Broadcast the supported case, stage a partisan night, sell an exclusive, expose the sponsor live or focus the programme on practical local work.
missions.consequences: A delivered programme gives the crew an editorial role and event access. The audience, sponsor and excluded faction remember what was actually said.
missions.next: AD7 Nia Sets the Terms · BM7 A Witness Chooses a Door · MR6 Buy the Frequency
missions.twist: One speaker brings an unsupported accusation and another brings genuine papers exposing the payer. Doors open after two preparation scenes.

missions.title: Nia Sets the Terms
missions.where: Willow Cabin · Approach Recovery Rooms · Evering Safe Flat
missions.hook: Leon has had a message: Nia will meet. Not the station, not the papers — the crew. Three factions have already offered her a car, cash or a bodyguard for her story.

objectives.text: Meet Nia at the Willow Cabin
Find independent support at the Approach Recovery Rooms
Get her to the Evering safe flat, and find out who pays for it
Deal with the faction driver and the better-funded offer
Decide: an independent account, an exclusive, a trade, exposure or a partial interview

missions.gm:
The job. A trusted intermediary offers a meeting with Nia. Rivals offer transport, cash and protection in exchange for her account.

Scenes. WW7.2 hosts the first conversation. BG8.3 supplies independent support or corroboration. SN8.2 is an onward refuge whose paying patron has not disclosed every term.

Route and checks. WW / HC / WS / BG / HR / LF / DA / SN. Front for competing offers; Wheels for transport; Bottle for a costly promise.
missions.decision: Back an independent account, negotiate an exclusive, trade evidence, expose her location or accept a partial interview and a smaller story.
missions.consequences: A meeting or authorised account confirms E4. The three private interiors open through the resulting relationships; betrayal can make Nia an active opponent with other allies.
missions.next: AD8 The Whole City Listening · RT7 Who Holds the Original · BM7 A Witness Chooses a Door
missions.twist: A faction driver arrives with a better-funded offer. If Nia leaves, she leaves a contact route rather than ending the case.

missions.title: The Whole City Listening
missions.where: Bridge Nine Broadcast Garage · The View Tube · Round Chapel · London Stadium
missions.hook: The Quiet Hour has begun. Patch is handing the crew the station's defining night: one broadcast that all of east London will hear. A sponsor, a street boss and a witness all want the same slot.

objectives.text: Take the mobile studio at the Bridge Nine Broadcast Garage
Collect the last account from the courier at the View Tube
Choose the broadcast site and name allies for the other
Hold the slot through three final-night turns
Decide what the city hears

missions.gm:
The job. Patch offers control of the station's defining night as the Quiet Hour begins. Other contested operations continue independently.

Scenes. ST8.2 allocates the mobile studio. A courier at BF2.3 brings the last account. HC2.2 or a fictional event wing at ST2.5 supplies the audience; choose one main broadcast site and named allies for the other.

Route and checks. ST / BF / OF / BG / WS / HC / WS / VW / ST. Front for live decisions; Graft for the rig; Bottle for the final offer.
missions.decision: Expose the scheme, sell silence, back a faction, stage a right of reply or trade airtime for concrete help.
missions.consequences: Gain the promised editorial stake or independent programme agreement. Record which studio the crew can use, who pays its next bill and who heard the account.
missions.next: RT8 A Record of What Happened · BM8 The Neighbourhood Gets a Vote · MR8 The City on the Brochure
missions.twist: A sponsor, a street boss and a witness want the same slot. Run three final-night turns with one interruption or competing emergency.

missions.title: Rent in Arrears
missions.where: Lea Bridge Social Rooms · The Gun · Shepherdess Coin Rooms
missions.hook: Moth has a collection that should be easy: a genuine debt, a household with a paid receipt — and another collector demanding the same money again.

objectives.text: Take Moth's brief at the Lea Bridge Social Rooms
Meet the debtor, the receipt and Daz at The Gun
Find the duplicate entry and the broker who sold it at the Shepherdess Coin Rooms
Decide: collect, buy the genuine debt, expose the duplicate or take the broker's cut

missions.gm:
The job. Moth offers a collection that should be easy: a genuine debt, a paid receipt and another collector demanding the money again.

Scenes. CL7.3 establishes Moth's brief. A fictional meeting in WS3.2 puts the debtor, receipt and Daz together. HX8.3 contains the duplicate entry and the broker who sold it.

Route and checks. CL / HC / WS / BG / HR / HX. Front for the debt; Savvy for records; Muscle or Bottle in the collection.
missions.decision: Collect by pressure, buy the genuine debt, expose the duplicate or take the broker's fee. Moth can accept a renegotiated settlement.
missions.consequences: The accepted account opens LB2 and the counting room. Each outcome creates named people who will help or oppose the crew; violence does not erase the receipt.
missions.next: LB2 Stretch Wants His Cut · BB1 A Small Balance · BM1 A Meal and a Receipt
missions.twist: Daz wants an example before the next round. The household has witnesses; the broker offers the crew a cut.

missions.title: Stretch Wants His Cut
missions.where: Bow Breakers Yard · Orient Night Shed · The Princess of Wales
missions.hook: Stretch says Pat's recovered van was carrying goods pledged to him, and he wants his cut. Moth wants it settled before the two crews start a proper feud.

objectives.text: See the yard contact at Bow Breakers
Identify the load and who paid for it at the Orient Night Shed
Stop Stretch's lieutenant moving the crate
Settle it at the meeting in The Princess of Wales
Decide: back Stretch, return Pat's share, steal the load or split it in front of witnesses

missions.gm:
The job. Stretch claims Pat's recovered van carried goods pledged to him. Moth wants the dispute settled before both crews begin a feud.

Scenes. EX-BREAKERS preserves the yard contact. HM7.4 identifies the load and the buyer who paid. CL2.2 hosts a fictional meeting beside the waiting courier.

Route and checks. OF / VW / WW / HM / CL. Wheels for the recovery; Graft for cargo; Front for rival claims.
missions.decision: Back Stretch, return Pat's share, steal the load for another buyer or divide it under a witnessed agreement.
missions.consequences: The agreed sponsor recognises the settlement. An unpaid claim survives a change of cargo ownership; HM7 remains a reachable recovery destination after a failed chase.
missions.next: LB3 The Larch Job · CH4 The Frame Room · TU2 The Van and the Debt
missions.twist: Stretch's lieutenant moves the crate toward a second vehicle. The first buyer demands a refund while a rival offers a recovery fee.

missions.title: The Larch Job
missions.where: The Crooked Billet · Larch Cold Store · Blue Hour Basement
missions.hook: A consignment of Halo is sitting in the Larch Cold Store waiting for Stretch's buyer. Moth wants it gone before he collects. Owen Pike will pay more if it ends up with his promoters instead.

objectives.text: Find out the pickup from the collector at The Crooked Billet
Get into the Larch Cold Store and reach the stock
Deal with the other crew when it arrives
Decide: deliver to Moth, sell to Owen at the Blue Hour Basement, keep it, trade it or have it withdrawn

missions.gm:
The job. Moth wants a valuable fictional Halo consignment stolen before Stretch's buyer collects it. Owen offers more for delivering it to his promoters.

Scenes. A fictional collector in CL3.2 identifies the pickup. LY8.2 to LY8.5 form a warehouse score: enter, reach the stock and confront another crew. DA8.5 is Owen's proposed cash-and-cargo exchange.

Route and checks. CL / HM / LY / HM / CL / HC / DA. Graft for the warehouse score; Muscle for the clash; Wheels for the load.
missions.decision: Deliver to Moth, sell to Owen, keep the stock, trade it to another faction or arrange its withdrawal for compensation.
missions.consequences: The patron rewards the agreed outcome. LY8 opens the damaging-batch mystery and DA8 opens the nightlife network; a discovered double sale creates a specific faction enemy.
missions.next: LB4 Halo With Teeth · VC4 The Last Good Batch · NM4 Protection by Post
missions.twist: The rival arrives after the crew commits. The announced vehicle handover puts the stock, a worker and an invoice at risk together.

missions.title: Halo With Teeth
missions.where: Approach Recovery Rooms · The Spread Eagle · Larch Cold Store · Majors
missions.hook: The consignment hurt people. Stretch wants the rest of the stock back. Moth thinks the Lea Boys were paid to take the blame for something somebody else changed.

objectives.text: Hear the harmed courier at the Approach Recovery Rooms
Find out about the earlier delivery at The Spread Eagle
Find the changed booking at the Larch Cold Store
Get the witness to hospital — Majors at Homerton A&E
Decide: carry on the trade, steal the stock, have it withdrawn or sell the proof of the switch

missions.gm:
The job. The consignment has harmed people. Stretch wants the remaining stock back; Moth suspects the organisation was paid to take the blame.

Scenes. BG8.3 introduces a harmed courier. A fictional meeting at WW4.2 identifies the agreed earlier delivery. LY8.5 holds the changed booking; AE3 can supply an independent hospital account.

Route and checks. BG / OF / VW / WW / HM / LY / HM / CL / HC. Savvy for the substitution; Front for rival briefs; Wheels for cargo or transport.
missions.decision: Continue the trade, steal the stock, arrange its withdrawal or sell evidence of the substitution.
missions.consequences: Accounts connect Owen and Rusk to the change. The trade outcome affects specific people and the Halo front; cooperation with one faction does not automatically tell every rival what happened.
missions.next: LB5 The Boy Who Kept Receipts · VC5 A Set for Nobody · BM4 After the Batch
missions.twist: A collector moves the remaining load while one witness needs hospital transport. Choose priorities and name any ally handling the other task.

missions.title: The Boy Who Kept Receipts
missions.where: The Coach and Horses · Well Street Loan Office · The Red Lion · Interview Room
missions.hook: A junior collector kept receipts — for debts that never existed. Stretch wants the book and the boy. Moth wants the book for herself, to use against Stretch.

objectives.text: Meet the seller at The Coach and Horses
Find the duplicate books at the Well Street Loan Office
Make (or spring) the handover at The Red Lion
Decide: deliver the book, deliver both, help the seller leave, sell it twice or take it to Vale

missions.gm:
The job. A junior collector has records of invented debts. Stretch wants both book and collector; Moth wants an account she can use against him.

Scenes. LY6.3 introduces the seller at a fictional meeting. WS8.4 holds duplicate books. SN4.2 offers a handover or ambush; CU4 provides a different route through Vale.

Route and checks. LY / HM / CL / HC / WS / HC / CL / SN. Front for terms; Graft for the ledger; Moves for an escort or pursuit.
missions.decision: Deliver the book, deliver both seller and book, help the seller leave, sell it twice or broker a supervised settlement.
missions.consequences: A recognised outcome advances its sponsor. The driver, duplicate records and new holder keep the trail active if the original handover fails.
missions.next: LB6 Terms From Above · BB5 Your Name in Someone Else's Book · LD4 Someone Else's Property
missions.page: LB5 · The Boy Who Kept Receipts
missions.twist: The seller has a ticket out and a rival following them. After two scenes, the book moves without a deal or contested recovery.

missions.title: Terms From Above
missions.where: North Park Hospitality Lodge · De Beauvoir Block · Quayline Records Suite
missions.hook: Stretch has shown the Lea Boys a partnership with Meridian Renewal: money, consultancy, a future. Moth asks the crew to find out what it costs before anyone commits.

objectives.text: Hear the offer at the North Park Hospitality Lodge
Find the consultancy invoice in the De Beauvoir Block suite
Sit in on Lark and the paying party at the Quayline Records Suite
Decide: back the deal, renegotiate, support Moth's split, sell the documents or take a fee of your own

missions.gm:
The job. Stretch reveals a profitable Meridian partnership. Moth asks the crew to discover its costs before members commit.

Scenes. ON8.3 presents the offer. An invented tenant's hired suite at DB3.3 holds the consultancy invoice. CG8.2 brings Lark and the paying party into one negotiation.

Route and checks. ON / ST / VW / WS / LF / DB / CG. Savvy for the account; Front for a counteroffer; Bottle against a lucrative future.
missions.decision: Back the deal, renegotiate, support Moth's split, sell the documents or take a consultancy fee of the crew's own.
missions.consequences: The sponsor recognises the accepted outcome. The property options become connected; a leak changes relations when traced or made public, while actual financial obligations survive.
missions.next: LB7 Who Speaks for the Lea Boys · MR6 Buy the Frequency · BB6 Land on Credit
missions.twist: Celia offers Stretch retirement while members expect continuing work and territory. The reception ends with a provisional commitment.

missions.title: Who Speaks for the Lea Boys
missions.where: York Hall · Lea Bridge Social Rooms · Hackney Marshes North Pavilion · MOTH Club
missions.hook: Moth is challenging Stretch's right to speak for the Lea Boys. The crew's standing could change who leads them — or split them in two.

objectives.text: Find the disputed pledge at the York Hall fight night
Gather the members' demands at the Lea Bridge Social Rooms
Protect the threatened runner at the Hackney Marshes North Pavilion
See the vote through at the MOTH Club
Decide who leads, who follows, and who walks — and name what each side keeps

missions.gm:
The job. Moth challenges Stretch's right to bind the faction. The crew's standing can change the leader or split the organisation.

Scenes. A fictional adult fight event at BG3.3 supplies a disputed pledge. CL7.2 gathers demands. HM1.4 introduces a threatened runner; a fictional vote in HC5.4 becomes the leadership set piece.

Route and checks. BG / WS / HC / CL / HM / CL / HC. Front for coalition building; Bottle for the challenge; Muscle if the meeting breaks down.
missions.decision: Keep Stretch, back Moth, take a leadership role, divide the faction or negotiate an exit. Name the members and assets supporting each camp.
missions.consequences: The chosen leadership offers LB8. Opponents survive through members, debts and witnesses; the crew gains a political position with concrete limits and responsibilities.
missions.next: LB8 The Price of a Patch · CH8 Keys to the Arches · BB8 The House Changes Hands
missions.page: LB7 · Who Speaks for the Lea Boys
missions.twist: Daz turns a genuine debt into a public humiliation. A fight gains attention while supporters weigh who will keep them paid.

missions.title: The Price of a Patch
missions.where: Clapton Union Rooms · Roman Exchange · Carpenters Breakfast Club · Meridian Sales Pavilion
missions.hook: The Quiet Hour is here. The Lea Boys can cash in on it, stand against it or sell part of the patch. What they become depends on the settlement their own people accept.

objectives.text: Hear the residents' claim at the Clapton Union Rooms
Bring the traders at Roman Exchange and the households at the Carpenters Breakfast Club
Face the investor meeting at the Meridian Sales Pavilion
Decide: a smaller street crew, a monopoly, Meridian's partner, or sell up and leave

missions.gm:
The job. The faction can exploit the Quiet Hour, resist it or sell part of its territory. Promotion depends on the settlement its supporters accept.

Scenes. CL8.3 establishes the residents' claim. OF7.2 supplies traders; BF8.3 supplies the household coalition. ST7.4 hosts the investor meeting and an offer to buy the core patch separately.

Route and checks. CL / HC / WS / BG / OF / BF / ST. Front for the settlement; Savvy for costs; Wheels for a contested delivery.
missions.decision: Build a smaller street crew, consolidate a monopoly, become Meridian's partner or sell the patch and leave.
missions.consequences: The final rank grants the agreed role or independent branch. Record its actual premises, income, creditors and opponents; real venues remain separately owned.
missions.next: MR8 The City on the Brochure · BM8 The Neighbourhood Gets a Vote · NM8 Who Gets a Place at the Table
missions.page: LB8 · The Price of a Patch
missions.twist: One offer saves the central business by abandoning another household. Collections, publicity and signatures continue on separate final-night turns.

missions.title: The Sound Went Missing
missions.where: Blue Hour Basement · Queensbridge Sound Store · Howling Hops Tank Bar
missions.hook: Owen's sound system went missing the week of his club night. The crew who moved it say he never paid for the hire in the first place — and a rival promoter has already paid for delivery.

objectives.text: Hear the promoter's version at the Blue Hour Basement
Find the changed booking at the Queensbridge Sound Store
Catch the replacement case at the Howling Hops Tank Bar before the van goes
Decide: steal back the rig, settle the hire bill, bring a smaller system or sell the booking

missions.gm:
The job. Owen wants a missing sound system recovered before an invented club night. The unpaid crew who moved it say he never paid for the original hire.

Scenes. DA8.3 gives the promoter's version. HR7.5 reveals the changed booking. A fictional visiting supplier at VW3.2 holds the replacement case while a van is loading.

Route and checks. DA / LF / HR / BG / OF / VW. Graft for equipment; Front for hire terms; Wheels for the van.
missions.decision: Steal back the rig, settle the hire bill, substitute a smaller system or sell the booking to the rival.
missions.consequences: An agreed recovery opens VC2 and repeat supplier access. A dishonest delivery earns criminal money while leaving a worker or buyer with proof of the debt.
missions.next: VC2 No Guest List for the Missing · AD1 Borrowed Speakers · TU1 The Wrong Case
missions.twist: A rival promoter has paid for immediate delivery. The hired driver has a genuine next job and leaves after two enquiries.

missions.title: No Guest List for the Missing
missions.where: Dalston Superstore · Theatre Royal Stratford East · Oslo Hackney
missions.hook: A performer has vanished off the bill a week before the show, and their costumes and kit are being held over a debt nobody can explain. Owen wants the show delivered. The performer might have other ideas.

objectives.text: Hear about the missing act from the promoter at Dalston Superstore
Find the disputed costume and the ultimatum at Theatre Royal Stratford East
Stop Harlan Black's man moving the belongings
Meet the performer and their supporter at Oslo Hackney
Decide: enforce the booking, bring them and their things home, broker an exit or take the rival fee

missions.gm:
The job. A performer vanishes from an invented show's bill while their belongings are held over an invented debt. Owen wants the performance delivered.

Route and checks. DA / HC / WS / VW / ST / ON / WW / HC. Front for labour and booking terms; Moves for pursuit; Muscle for a contested recovery.
missions.decision: Enforce the booking, recover the performer and property, broker an exit or take a replacement fee from the rival.
missions.consequences: The agreed promoter rewards the outcome. Harlan becomes an independent antagonist if crossed; the performer can become a contact, rival or witness without belonging to Meridian's scheme.
missions.next: VC3 Cash Before Curtain · GE2 The Coat With the Appointment · RT2 The Watch After Midnight
missions.page: VC2 · No Guest List for the Missing
missions.twist: Harlan Black's hired enforcer is moving the belongings before the final rehearsal. The performer has a plan of their own and a rival employer's offer.

missions.title: Cash Before Curtain
missions.where: Clapton Country Club · Hackney Empire · Leyton Great Hall · The Eagle
missions.hook: The headline act at Owen's benefit hasn't been paid, and the case of advances has gone walkabout. Owen will pay the crew to protect his programme — and, he doesn't say, his books.

objectives.text: Find out what the workers were promised at Clapton Country Club
Trace the missing cash case at the Hackney Empire
Get into the payer's private gala at Leyton Great Hall
Get the receipt Owen hoped nobody kept, from the organiser at The Eagle
Decide before the first speech: recover the cash, steal it, expose the missing fee or cut the bill

missions.gm:
The job. A fictional benefit has an unpaid principal act and a case of missing advances. Owen will pay the crew to protect his programme and his account.

Scenes. CL5.4 establishes what workers were promised. HC1.5 identifies the missing cash case. LY4.3 hosts the payer's private gala; a visiting organiser at HX2.3 holds the receipt Owen hoped nobody kept.

Route and checks. CL / HC / CL / HM / LY / HM / CL / HC / DA / CG / DB / HX. Graft for the case; Front for the settlement; Bottle before the curtain.
missions.decision: Recover the cash, steal it for the crew, expose the missing fee, credit a different sponsor or forge ahead with an agreed smaller bill.
missions.consequences: A supported account opens the wider finance trail. The chosen settlement keeps a show running or creates an unpaid claim that follows Owen and the crew into later jobs.
missions.next: VC4 The Last Good Batch · BB3 Cash on the Guest List · AD6 Open Channel Loud Mouths
missions.twist: The act refuses the first entrance while a rival moves the case between the gala's rooms. The first public speech is the deadline.

missions.title: The Last Good Batch
missions.where: Larch Cold Store · Approach Recovery Rooms · Number 90

objectives.text: Find the disputed stock in the Larch Cold Store
Hear an independent account of the harm at the Approach Recovery Rooms
Walk into the cash meeting at Number 90 with Owen's agent and the rival buyer
Decide: deliver the stock, have it withdrawn, take the rival fee or trade the records

The job. Owen calls a disputed Halo shipment a theft. A supplier says its contents were changed, and a rival offers a premium for whatever remains.

Scenes. LY8.3 contains the disputed stock. BG8.2 supplies an independent account of the harm. A fictional cash meeting at VW5.4 brings Owen's agent and the rival buyer into the same room.

Route and checks. LY / HM / CL / HC / WS / BG / OF / VW. Graft for cargo; Savvy for the change; Front for the buyers.
missions.decision: Deliver the stock, arrange its withdrawal, take the rival's fee or trade its accompanying records for a more valuable concession.
missions.consequences: The accepted brief earns its sponsor's award. Evidence supports the deliberate substitution; continuing the trade creates specific harm and opposition rather than a cost-free abstract reward.
missions.next: VC5 A Set for Nobody · LB4 Halo With Teeth · BM4 After the Batch

missions.title: A Set for Nobody
missions.where: The Shacklewell Arms · North Echo Rehearsal Rooms · Englefield Listening Flat

Get the rehearsal version at the North Echo Rehearsal Rooms
Find the old ident, and who reused it, at the Englefield Listening Flat
Survive the contested handover at the private listening
Decide: sell the rough mix, keep a copy, deliver it to Owen or bargain for a release

The job. An unreleased set undermines the supposed Halo warning. Owen wants it returned and its visiting performer wants it preserved.

missions.decision: Sell the rough mix, preserve a copy, deliver it to Owen or bargain for a limited public release.
missions.consequences: An authenticated version supports E3. Losing one original leaves the rehearsal and Leon's account, while the buyer who holds it gains a new lever over the next event.
missions.next: VC6 The Sponsor Behind the Sponsor · AD5 Somebody Else's Voice · RT4 The Night That Repeated

missions.title: The Sponsor Behind the Sponsor

Find the reception account at The Stratford hotel
Meet the real guarantor at The Baring
Give your answer at the sponsor briefing, North Park Hospitality Lodge
Decide: transparent funding, sell control, take a share, expose the guarantor or build a small coalition

The job. Meridian offers to make Owen its official nightlife partner. He wants the crew's endorsement while hiding his financial connection.

Route and checks. WS / HC / WW / ON / ST / BF / OF / BG / HR / HX / DB / CG / DA / HC / WW / ON. Front for the contract; Savvy for accounts; Bottle when the crew is offered a cut.
missions.decision: Back transparent funding, sell control, demand a share, expose the guarantor or find a smaller independent coalition.

missions.next: VC7 Last Dance Before the Sale · MR6 Buy the Frequency · BB6 Land on Credit

missions.title: Last Dance Before the Sale

objectives.text: Secure the production hire at the ABBA Arena
Bring in the principal act at Sadler's Wells East
Get the returning cases to EartH
Find where Owen's courier went in the rough cut at 3 Mills Studios
Decide what happens to Owen and his book: witness, recovery, sale or a compromised partner

missions.gm:
The job. A fictional benefit programme could keep the circuit independent. Owen is trying to leave with the account book before the final performance.

missions.next: VC8 Who Owns the Night · LD7 Four Notices Before Midnight · GE7 The Collection That Can Speak
missions.page: VC7 · Last Dance Before the Sale

missions.title: Who Owns the Night

Allocate the last deliveries at the Marshgate Delivery Depot
Make the new ownership public at the London Stadium programme
Decide: a promoters' cooperative, criminal control, corporate money, a split or sell your stake

missions.gm:
The job. The circuit offers the crew a share in its future while Owen's account sits at the centre of several final-night bargains.

missions.gm:
The offer. A fictional performer loses a jacket containing a small inheritance and a first-night cue. A rival wears an identical jacket and denies the theft.

The truth (GM). A wardrobe assistant mixed the jackets during a borrowed private costume session. An adult guest pocketed the envelope afterward and is trying to spend the money at a second event.

Scenes. Check the temporary costume stand in ST1.3, compare the garments in ST4.5 and confront the guest at a fictional workshop in ST6.4. The cue can be reconstructed even if the cash is gone.

missions.twist: The first performance begins after the second appointment. A replacement jacket saves the show while a witness can still identify the guest later.

The offer. A family wants a cabinet returned before a fictional lender sells its contents. Frankie claims it was a voluntary repayment.

Scenes. Hear the family in HX1.2, find the second collector during a private theatre booking in HX3.5 and examine the actual account in HX8.3. The family can identify the watch's owner if shown it.

missions.gm:
The offer. Retired cabdriver Arthur Venn hears that a fictional memorial benefit has been arranged in his name. He hires the crew to discover who is collecting the money.

The truth (GM). An adult former colleague has invented Arthur's death to pay a private gambling debt. A visiting promoter believed the story and has booked an unusual evening programme.

Scenes. Meet Arthur and the booking volunteer in BG4.3, confront the promoter during a hired gathering in BG6.3 and compare the supposed obituary with the real club newsletter in BG5.4. Arthur decides how publicly to reveal that he is alive.

missions.page: S18 · The Funeral for a Living Cabbie
missions.twist: The benefit starts after two enquiries. The debtor collects the cash at the interval, creating a public confrontation or a later recovery.

missions.title: The Bell in the Wrong Crate
missions.where: Nunnery Gallery · Forman's Fish Island · Roman Exchange
missions.hook: A valuable stage bell arrived at the market in a crate with a stagehand's bloodstained coat. The stagehand, Perry Sloane, was found dead offstage. This one is a murder.

objectives.text: Compare the crate record at the Nunnery Gallery
Question Len Fisk at the Forman's gathering
Intercept the bell at the Roman Exchange
Decide who gets the truth about Perry — and what happens to Len

missions.gm:
The offer. Pearl hires the crew after a valuable stage bell arrives in a crate containing adult stagehand Perry Sloane's bloodstained coat. Perry has been found dead offstage.

The truth (GM). Fictional reseller Len Fisk killed Perry after Perry discovered Len's separate resale fraud. This is an independent murder, not a Meridian order or another version of Nia's disappearance.

Scenes. Compare the hired exhibition's crate record in OF2.5, question Len at a private gathering in OF6.3 and intercept his attempted disposal in OF7.4. A witness identifies the quarrel without needing a successful roll; rolls determine speed and the price of cooperation.

Atlas route. OF (one district: every scene is on this street map)
missions.consequences: Recover the bell and decide who receives the supported account, sell a truthful ownership claim or conceal the killer for a stated criminal price. GBP 240 and 1 NM or LD Renown once for the disclosed commission; concealing Len makes Perry's family a continuing opposition.
missions.page: S19 · The Bell in the Wrong Crate
missions.twist: Len tries to sell the bell after the second interview. If warned, he flees to a buyer already listed in the ledger, creating a follow-up pursuit.

missions.title: The Film with the Missing Van
missions.where: 3 Mills Studios · Pudding Mill Lane DLR station · Marshgate Delivery Depot
missions.hook: A student film crew caught something in the background of a shot: a van, a performer named Mara Sol, and a handover she clearly didn't want. Tern wants her found before one of the drivers is blamed.

objectives.text: Get consent to view the rushes at 3 Mills Studios
Meet the driver at Pudding Mill Lane
Intercept Harlan Black's delivery at the Marshgate depot
Decide with Mara: recover, buy out and fight the debt, or seize Black's leverage

missions.gm:
The offer. A fictional student production accidentally records a coercive van handover involving adult performer Mara Sol. Tern wants the passenger found before a hired driver is blamed.

The truth (GM). Independent criminal Harlan Black is forcing Mara to work off a fabricated private debt. The footage is separate from the Meridian plot, and Mara wants her friend released from another obligation as well.

Scenes. Obtain the filmmakers' consent to view the rushes in BF4.4, meet the driver at BF6.2 and intercept Black's fictional delivery in BF7.2. Mara has her own plan and can help bargain, escape or expose Black.

Atlas route. BF (one district: every scene is on this street map)
missions.consequences: Recover the passenger, buy out and then contest the debt, or seize Black's payment leverage. GBP 240 and 1 TU or VC Renown once; Mara chooses future bookings independently and can become a recurring contact.
missions.page: S20 · The Film with the Missing Van
missions.twist: Black moves the van after the second enquiry. A station witness has the next paid destination if the crew misses it; a failed interception changes the rendezvous rather than removing Mara from play.
